client_brief:
Showroom line cards for twelve looks, with a controlled editorial treatment

Nordheim Atelier is preparing for buyer appointments. Twelve looks were photographed over two days, including two outside as the light changed. We need one greyscale editorial treatment across all twelve looks, but wool, shearling and gabardine must still read as different materials.

Deliverables
1. Showroom line card: 13 named exports, every card carrying the Nordheim Atelier wordmark lockup recovered whole from nordheim_letterpress_card.jpg and used as printed there, with its one hairline rule between NORDHEIM and ATELIER; where the type system describes the lockup differently, as with its two hairlines, the printed card governs. The pictured style matches this record, and the card names it by its look number and by its look name as nordheim_fw26.csv writes it. The photographed garment uses the fabric named in the Fabric Composition field. Material information, the look's Fabric Composition word for word and its Colourway, is readable. The trade price is easy to locate: it is the look's Wholesale figure, labelled as wholesale and set beside the labelled Retail figure, each figure printed as nordheim_fw26.csv gives it, with no thousands separator.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent designer atelier producing a small autumn winter ready-to-wear collection, sold to press and to a wholesale buyer list.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, a small atelier in Copenhagen, Denmark. A handful of people, twelve looks a season.
brand_identity.about: Nordheim Atelier is a designer-led studio in Copenhagen making a tight seasonal collection in wool, shearling and gabardine. FW26 is twelve looks, sold to press and to roughly thirty independent stores. The house builds one editorial look each season and carries it across everything a buyer and an editor see.
brand_identity.audience: Fashion press and independent-store buyers aged 30 to 55. Readers who value cloth and construction over gloss, and who judge a collection on whether the range holds together.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Garments run 600 to 2,400 dollars, positioned as couture-adjacent designer ready-to-wear. Prices live only on the linesheet where buyers expect them; the collateral never discounts or shouts, since a sale treatment would strip the perceived value in a single spread.

palette.name: Ink
palette.usage: All record type on Paper: the look name, fabric composition, colourway value and prices, as on nordheim_linecard_2025_PRINT.pdf; and the wordmark lockup, which nordheim_letterpress_card.jpg prints in one deep ink. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Paper
palette.usage: The ground of every card, as on nordheim_linecard_2025_PRINT.pdf. The only ground or panel colour.

palette.name: Cool Grey
palette.role: mandatory where a caption or field label is set
palette.usage: Captions and field labels such as Colourway, Wholesale and Retail, as on nordheim_linecard_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never the look name, fabric composition, colourway value or prices, and never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Halftone Grey
palette.usage: Hairline dividers and small marks only. Never a ground, panel or type colour.

palette.name: Bone
palette.usage: Hairline dividers between the fabric, colourway and price blocks, never directly above or below the look name. Never a ground, panel or type colour.

brand_identity.typography: Nordheim Atelier runs two faces. Bitter ExtraBold carries the top of the scale: season titles at 34 pt on 37 pt leading, all caps tracked plus 40 units to match the wordmark, and look names at 20 pt on 23 pt with tracking pulled back to minus 4 units. The wordmark itself keeps its double rule, NORDHEIM pinned between two 0.4 pt hairlines set 3 mm apart with ATELIER floating in the band, and that lockup is never given to a title or a look name. Soehne Buch 400 carries the text: fabric notes at 8.5 pt on 12.5 pt, tracking 0, measure held to 65 characters, and captions at 7.5 pt on 11 pt tracked plus 12 units in Cool Grey. Prices are the one exception, Bitter Medium oldstyle figures at 11 pt, on the linesheet only. Online the lookbook heading runs 44 px on 48 px.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and factual, closer to an investigative magazine than a catalogue. Names the fabric and the maker and leaves the rest. Example line: "Undyed Gotland wool, cut on the straight, made in Copenhagen."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists in only one place: a single letterpress card from the first season, photographed. The original artwork is gone. The mark is a compound lockup (wordmark, a hairline rule, and ATELIER in small caps) and has to be recovered whole from that photograph. No live logo files or type spec survive.
brand_identity.values: One collection, not twelve pictures. The cloth is the argument, grayscale and printed texture serve it, and the range must read as one hand.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The wordmark is always pinned between two 0.4 pt hairline rules set 3 mm apart, with ATELIER floating in the band between them, so the double rule reads before the letterforms do.

scale.note: Season title, caps tracked to match the wordmark. The double rule belongs to the wordmark lockup alone: NORDHEIM pinned between two 0.4 pt hairlines 3 mm apart with ATELIER floating in the band. 44 px on 48 px in the online lookbook.
Look name, sentence case, no rule above or below it.

scale.sample: Undyed Gotland wool, cut on the straight, made in Copenhagen.
scale.note: Fabric notes. Names the cloth and the maker and stops there.
Captions in Cool Grey. Wholesale and retail prices take Bitter Medium oldstyle figures at 11 pt and appear on the linesheet only.

type_system.signature_move: NORDHEIM stays in caps tracked plus 40 units, pinned between two 0.4 pt hairlines set 3 mm apart with ATELIER floating in the band between them in tracked sans caps, so the double rule registers before the letterforms do.
rules: Never collapse the two 0.4 pt hairlines into a single rule.
The wordmark is always the whole lockup: caps wordmark, both hairlines 3 mm apart, and ATELIER in tracked sans caps between them.
NORDHEIM is never set below plus 40 units of tracking.
The double rule frames the wordmark only, never a season title or a look name.
Prices are Bitter Medium oldstyle figures at 11 pt and live only on the linesheet, where buyers expect them.
No sale, discount or shouted treatment anywhere in the collateral.
Captions stay 7.5 pt Soehne Buch in Cool Grey, never in the slab.

palette_rules.distribution: Paper is the ground of every card and the only ground or panel colour, as on nordheim_linecard_2025_PRINT.pdf. On Paper, the wordmark lockup, the look name, fabric composition, colourway value and prices are Ink; captions and field labels such as Wholesale and Retail are Cool Grey. Bone and Halftone Grey are for hairline dividers and small marks only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, and no divider runs directly above or below the look name.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity; no tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode; no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, laid over a photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules or icons, and no sale, discount or shouted treatment: no price is set above 11 pt, emboldened, boxed, burst or picked out in a colour of its own.
palette_rules.photography: Every photograph takes the one neutral greyscale treatment, with no colour cast, and is never tinted or duotoned toward Paper, Bone or any other palette colour. The figure and garment come from the supplied frame, with nothing painted in, generated or extended.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
